data.name: Dharam
data.gender_notes: Dharam is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dharam is a name derived from the Sanskrit term 'dharma', which means 'righteousness', 'duty', and 'morality'. It is an essential concept in Hinduism and Buddhism, emphasizing ethical conduct and living a virtuous life according to one's duty or role in society. The name Dharam carries the meaning “Dharma (righteousness, duty)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dharam usually hope their child will grow to embody dharma (righteousness, duty) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies one's connection to the divine duty and righteous path in life.
data.etymology: Dharam belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dharma (righteousness, duty).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dharam total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_sanskrit.meaning: Dharma, righteousness, duty, law, moral values
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The term Dharma denotes the fundamental law of the universe, the natural order of things, and the right way of living for human beings. It is a concept that encompasses various aspects of life such as righteousness, duty, morality, and law. In Hinduism, Dharma is considered one of the four goals of human life, along with Artha (prosperity), Kama (desire), and Moksha (liberation).
